questions.question: The famous 'Chilka Lake' is located in which state?
questions.questionHtml: The famous 'Chilka Lake' is located in which state?
questions.solution: Chilka Lake, a famous brackish water lagoon, is located in Odisha. It is the largest coastal lagoon in India and the second-largest in the world. Known for its rich biodiversity, it serves as a significant habitat for migratory birds and supports local fishing communities.

questions.question: The book 'The Presidential Years' has been written by whom?
questions.questionHtml: The book 'The Presidential Years' has been written by whom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Pranab Mukherjee.

Key Points

  • The book 'The Presidential Years' has been written by Pranab Mukherjee.
  • Pranab Mukherjee was an Indian politician who served as the 13th President of India from 2012 until 2017.
  • He was Union Finance Minister from 2009 to 2012.
  • He served as the 13th President of India from 25 July 2012 to 25 July 2017
  • He was awarded India's highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna, in 2019, by the President of India, Ram Nath Kovind.
  • The presidential years give a fascinating account of how one of the country's most respected veteran politicians reshaped the functioning of Rashtrapati Bhavan and responded to tumultuous events as the country's first citizen, leaving behind a legacy that will be hard to match.

Additional Information

Books written by other authors are:

Author Books
Dr Abdul Kalam
  • Wings of fire
  • Ignited Minds
  • Turning Points
K. R. Narayanan
  • Image and Insights
  • Nehru and his vision
Dr. Shankardayal Sharma
  • Chetna ke Shrot
  • Deshmani
  • Eminent Indians

 

Mistake Points

  • My Presidential Years was written by R Venkataraman.
  • My Presidential Years, which covered the highly charged years 1987–1992, is a first-person account of the events of R Venkataraman's time as India's eighth president. Never before has an Indian president's term been so eventful, difficult, and demanding.

questions.question: __________ ​is a device used for measuring the optical activity exhibited by inorganic and organic compounds.
questions.questionHtml: __________ ​is a device used for measuring the optical activity exhibited by inorganic and organic compounds.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Polarimeter

Key Points

  • Polarimeter is a scientific instrument used to measure the angle of rotation caused by passing polarized light through an optically active substance.
  • It is commonly used to measure the optical activity exhibited by inorganic and organic compounds.
  • Optical activity refers to the ability of certain substances to rotate the plane of polarized light.
  • Polarimeters are widely used in the fields of chemistry, biochemistry, and pharmaceuticals to determine the concentration and purity of optically active substances.

Additional Information

  • Photometer is an instrument for measuring the intensity of light.
  • Ammeter is used to measure electric current in a circuit.
  • Centrifuge is a device that uses centrifugal force to separate components of a mixture based on their densities.
  • Polarimetry is a valuable technique in the food industry for determining the sugar content in products like honey and fruit juices.

questions.question: What is the theme of World Cancer Day 2025-27?
questions.questionHtml: What is the theme of World Cancer Day 2025-27?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is United by Unique.

In News

  • World Cancer Day 2025 is observed on February 4th, commemorating 25 years of the Charter of Paris Against Cancer.

Key Points

  • The theme for World Cancer Day 2025-27 is "United by Unique," emphasizing collective commitment against cancer.
  • World Cancer Day was first observed on February 4, 2000, during the World Summit Against Cancer for the New Millennium in Paris.
  • The Charter of Paris Against Cancer was signed 25 years ago, reinforcing the global fight against cancer.
  • The event raises awareness and promotes global efforts in cancer prevention, diagnosis, and treatment.

Additional Information

  • World Cancer Day: A global initiative led by the **Union for International Cancer Control (UICC)** to create awareness and promote action against cancer.
  • Charter of Paris Against Cancer: Signed in **2000**, it outlines 10 key commitments for improving cancer care and research.
  • Global Impact: The initiative aims to **reduce the global cancer burden, ensure equal access to treatment, and improve survival rates**.
  • Previous Themes: Past themes included **"I Am and I Will" (2019-2021)** and **"Close the Care Gap" (2022-2024)**, highlighting different aspects of cancer awareness.

questions.question: Consider the following statements comparing the Simon Commission (1927) and the Nehru Report (1928): 1. The Simon Commission was boycotted by Indian political parties primarily due to its all-Indian composition. 2. The Nehru Report proposed complete independence for India as its immediate objective. Which of the above is / are correct?
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the following statements comparing the Simon Commission (1927) and the Nehru Report (1928):

1. The Simon Commission was boycotted by Indian political parties primarily due to its all-Indian composition.

2. The Nehru Report proposed complete independence for India as its immediate objective.

Which of the above is / are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Neither 1 nor 2.

Key Points

  • Statement 1 is incorrect: The Simon Commission (1927) was boycotted by Indian political parties primarily because it lacked any Indian representation, not because of its "all-Indian composition." The commission consisted solely of British members, leading to widespread protests.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: The Nehru Report (1928), authored by Motilal Nehru, advocated for "Dominion Status" for India within the British Empire, not complete independence. The demand for complete independence was officially adopted later in 1929 during the Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress.
  • The Simon Commission was tasked with reviewing the Government of India Act, 1919, and recommending constitutional reforms, but it was met with hostility due to its exclusion of Indians from the process.
  • The Nehru Report marked a significant effort by Indian leaders to draft a constitution for self-governance, but it fell short of the aspirations of younger leaders like Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Chandra Bose, who sought complete independence.

Additional Information

  • Simon Commission (1927):
    • Officially known as the Indian Statutory Commission, it was led by Sir John Simon and consisted entirely of British members, which was a major point of contention.
    • Its arrival in India was met with protests and slogans like "Simon Go Back." Leaders like Lala Lajpat Rai played a key role in opposing it.
    • The commission's recommendations eventually led to the Government of India Act, 1935.
  • Nehru Report (1928):
    • This was the first attempt by Indians to draft a constitutional framework for India.
    • It proposed a parliamentary system of governance, protection of minority rights, and fundamental rights but fell short of demanding complete independence.
    • Its rejection by the British and the failure to meet the aspirations of younger leaders led to a shift in Congress's stance toward the demand for complete independence.
  • Lahore Session (1929):
    • In this session, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, the Indian National Congress officially adopted "Purna Swaraj" (Complete Independence) as its goal.
    • 26th January 1930 was declared as Independence Day, which is now celebrated as Republic Day in remembrance of this declaration.
  • Government of India Act, 1935:
    • This act was influenced by the Simon Commission's recommendations and introduced provincial autonomy and the federal structure in India.
    • It served as a precursor to India's constitutional development leading up to independence.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct related to respiration? (i) In alveoli, exchange of gases takes place. (ii) The walls of alveoli contain an extensive network of blood vessel. (iii) In human beings, the respiratory pigments is haemoglobin.
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following statements is/are correct related to respiration?

(i) In alveoli, exchange of gases takes place.

(ii) The walls of alveoli contain an extensive network of blood vessel.

(iii) In human beings, the respiratory pigments is haemoglobin.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is (i), (ii) and (iii).

Key Points

  • In alveoli, exchange of gases takes place. Oxygen diffuses from the alveoli into the blood, while carbon dioxide diffuses from the blood into the alveoli.
  • The walls of the alveoli contain an extensive network of blood vessels, primarily capillaries, which facilitate the exchange of gases.
  • Haemoglobin is the respiratory pigment in human beings. It is a protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body.
  • The alveoli are tiny air sacs within the lungs where the process of external respiration occurs.

Additional Information

  • Alveoli
    • The human lungs contain approximately 300 million alveoli, providing a large surface area for gas exchange.
    • Alveoli are lined with a thin layer of epithelial cells and are surrounded by capillaries to facilitate efficient gas exchange.
  • Haemoglobin
    • Haemoglobin is a complex protein containing iron, which binds to oxygen molecules.
    • Each haemoglobin molecule can carry up to four oxygen molecules.
    • Haemoglobin also plays a role in transporting carbon dioxide from tissues back to the lungs.
  • Respiratory System
    • The human respiratory system consists of the nasal cavity, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi, and lungs.
    • It is responsible for taking in oxygen and expelling carbon dioxide.
    • The diaphragm and intercostal muscles play a crucial role in the process of breathing.

questions.questionHtml: Which Article in the fundamental duty applies, when a construction worker takes his 8-year son to the site rather than sending him to school?

questions.question: Who instituted the land revenue system named Dahsala ?
questions.questionHtml: Who instituted the land revenue system named Dahsala ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Akbar.

Key Points

  • The Dahsala system, also known as the Zabti system, was introduced by Akbar in 1580-82 AD.
  • This system was developed by Raja Todar Mal, Akbar's finance minister, to streamline land revenue collection.
  • It fixed the average produce and prices of crops over the last 10 years and calculated one-third of the average as the state's share.
  • The system was aimed at ensuring fairness in taxation and reducing exploitation of farmers by intermediaries.

Additional Information

  • Iltutmish: Iltutmish was the third ruler of the Slave Dynasty and is credited with consolidating the Delhi Sultanate. He introduced the silver Tanka and copper Jital coins but had no association with land revenue reforms like Dahsala.
  • Sher Shah: Sher Shah Suri introduced an early form of land revenue reforms known as the Ryotwari system. He is also known for establishing the Grand Trunk Road and reforming the postal system.
  • Aurangzeb: Aurangzeb was the last significant Mughal emperor and is known for his orthodox policies. He imposed the Jizya tax on non-Muslims and expanded the Mughal Empire, but he did not introduce the Dahsala system.

questions.question: Which of the following national movement is also known as 'August Revolution'?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following national movement is also known as 'August Revolution'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Quit India Movement.

Key Points

Quit India Movement (1942):

  • On 8th August 1942, Mahatma Gandhi called to end British rule and launched the Quit India Movement at the session of the All-India Congress Committee in Mumbai.
  • This movement is also known as the India August Movement or August Kranti.
  • Gandhiji gave the call “Do or Die” in his speech delivered at the Gowalia Tank Maidan, now popularly known as August Kranti Maidan.
  • Aruna Asaf Ali popularly known as the 'Grand Old Lady' of the Independence Movement is known for hoisting the Indian flag at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Mumbai during the Quit India Movement.
  • The slogan ‘Quit India’ was coined by Yusuf Meherally, a socialist and trade unionist who also served as Mayor of Mumbai.
  • The Quit India Resolution was passed by the Congress Working Committee on 8 August 1942 in Bombay. Gandhi was named the movement’s leader.
  • The resolution stated the provisions of the movement as:
    • An immediate end to British rule over India.
    • Declaration of the commitment of free India to defend itself against all kinds of imperialism and fascism.
    • Formation of a provisional government of India after British withdrawal.
    • Sanctioning a civil disobedience movement against British rule.

questions.question: Harihara I was the ruler of which Dynasty?
questions.questionHtml: Harihara I was the ruler of which Dynasty?
questions.solution: Harihara I and his brother Bukka founded the Vijayanagara empire and established the Sangama dynasty. They built the city of Vijayanagara and implemented a successful system of administration that lasted until the end of the empire. Harihara I also promoted agriculture and fortified several forts.

questions.question: Under the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) Yojana, a monthly pension of _______ rupees will be provided to the employees of unorganised sector after 60 years of age.
questions.questionHtml: Under the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) Yojana, a monthly pension of _______ rupees will be provided to the employees of unorganised sector after 60 years of age.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 3000.

Key Points

Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan:

  • It is a central government scheme meant for old age protection and social security of Unorganised Workers (UW). 
  • Unorganised Workers (UW) are mostly engaged as rickshaw pullers, street vendors, mid-day meal workers, head loaders, brick kiln workers, cobblers, rag pickers, domestic workers, washermen, home-based workers, own-account workers, agricultural workers, construction workers, beedi workers, handloom workers, leather workers, audio-visual workers or in similar other occupations.
    • There are an estimated 42 crore, such unorganised workers, in the country.
  • Eligibility:
    • Should be an unorganised worker (UW).
    • Belong to the list of professions listed by the government.
    • Entry age between 18 and 40 years.
    • Monthly Income Rs 15000 or below.
  • Should not be:
    • Engaged in Organized Sector (membership of EPF/NPS/ESIC).
    • An income taxpayer
  • He/ She should possess an Aadhar card Savings Bank Account / Jan Dhan account number with IFSC.
  • Features:
    • It is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme, under which the subscriber would receive a minimum assured pension of Rs 3000/- per month after attaining the age of 60 years and if the subscriber dies, the spouse of the beneficiary shall be entitled to receive 50% of the pension as family pension.
      • Family pension is applicable only to spouses.
    • Payment of pension by LIC.
    • The Central Government will also give an equal matching contribution in his pension account.
